claim: The accessory olfactory system (AOS) mediates specialized chemosensory signals that elicit innate social behaviors in individuals of several vertebrate species.
source: Specialized chemosensory signals elicit innate social behaviors in individuals of several vertebrate species, a process that is mediated via the accessory olfactory system (AOS).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental data from this study.

claim: The study performed single-cell transcriptomics of the mouse vomeronasal sensory epithelium.
source: To gain insight into the cell types, developmental gene expression patterns, and functional differences amongst neurons, we performed single-cell transcriptomics of the mouse vomeronasal sensory epithelium.
evidence: The methods section describes the experimental procedures for single-cell RNA sequencing.

claim: The analysis reveals diverse cell types with gene expression patterns specific to each.
source: Our analysis reveals diverse cell types with gene expression patterns specific to each, which we made available as a searchable web resource accessed from https://www.scvnoexplorer.com.
evidence: Figure 1 shows UMAP clustering of different cell types with specific markers.

claim: Neurons originating from common progenitors diverge in their gene expression during maturation with transient and persistent transcription factor expression at critical branch points.
source: Pseudo-time developmental analysis indicates that neurons originating from common progenitors diverge in their gene expression during maturation with transient and persistent transcription factor expression at critical branch points.
evidence: Figure 3 shows pseudotime trajectory analysis and differential expression of transcription factors during development.

claim: Gnao1 neurons have significantly higher expression of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) associated genes compared to Gnai2 neurons.
source: Comparative analysis across two of the major neuronal subtypes that express divergent GPCR families and the G-protein subunits Gnai2 or Gnao1, reveals significantly higher expression of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) associated genes within Gnao1 neurons.
evidence: Figure 6A shows GO enrichment analysis of ER-related terms in Gnao1 neurons, and Figure 6B shows RNA-ISH validation.

claim: Gnao1 neurons show differences in ER content and prevalence of cubic membrane ER ultrastructure compared to Gnai2 neurons.
source: In addition, differences in ER content and prevalence of cubic membrane ER ultrastructure revealed by electron microscopy, indicate fundamental differences in ER function.
evidence: Figure 8 shows electron microscopy images revealing cubic membrane ER structures in Gnao1 neurons.

claim: V1R and V2R expressing neurons are spatially segregated within the neuroepithelium.
source: V1R and V2R expressing neurons are spatially segregated within the neuroepithelium, and project to distinct locations in the accessory olfactory bulb along the anterior-posterior axis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge without specific experimental data from this study.

claim: V1R and V2R neurons project to distinct locations in the accessory olfactory bulb along the anterior-posterior axis.
source: V1R and V2R expressing neurons are spatially segregated within the neuroepithelium, and project to distinct locations in the accessory olfactory bulb along the anterior-posterior axis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge without specific experimental data from this study.

claim: Functional evidence suggests that V1R and V2R neurons may recognize ligands that mediate different behaviors.
source: Functional evidence suggests that V1R and V2R neurons may recognize ligands that mediate different behaviors (Chamero et al., 2011; Oboti et al., 2014; Trouillet et al., 2019; Pallé et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Cognate ligand binding in both Gnao1 and Gnai2 neurons is thought to signal via the phospholipase-c pathway which results in the activation of the VNO-specific cation channel, Trpc2.
source: Cognate ligand binding in both Gnao1 and Gnai2 neurons, is thought to signal via the phospholipase-c pathway which results in the activation of the VNO-specific cation channel, Trpc2 (Liman et al., 1999; Stowers et al., 2002; Zufall, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the main olfactory epithelium (MOE), neurons regenerate throughout life, continuously differentiating from a stem cell population into neurons and supporting cell types.
source: In the main olfactory epithelium (MOE), neurons regenerate throughout life, continuously differentiating from a stem cell population into neurons and supporting cell types (Fletcher et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Neuronal differentiation in the MOE is associated with the expression of a single GPCR to the exclusion of many others.
source: Neuronal differentiation is also associated with the expression of a single GPCR to the exclusion of many others (Hanchate et al., 2015; Tan et al., 2015), leading to the hallmark feature termed as 'one neuron one receptor (ONOR)' rule (Malnic et al., 1999; Serizawa et al., 2000; Serizawa et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: VNO sensory neurons continuously regenerate from a stem cell population.
source: VNO sensory neurons (VSNs) also continuously regenerate (Barber and Raisman, 1978; Wilson and Raisman, 1980) from a stem cell population, and differentiating cells take on the identity of supporting cells and mature neurons of either the Gnao1 or Gnai2 sub-types (Katreddi et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Gnai2 neurons largely follow the ONOR rule in expressing one V1R gene per neuron.
source: While Gnai2 neurons seem to largely follow the ONOR rule in expressing one V1R gene per neuron (Serizawa et al., 2004), Gnao1 neurons seemingly deviate from this rule by co-expressing a combination of GPCRs.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Each Gnao1 neuron expresses a single V2R gene from the ABD family as well as a member of the C family V2R genes.
source: Thus, each Gnao1 neuron expresses a single V2R gene from the ABD family as well as a member of the C family V2R genes (Martini et al., 2001; Silvotti et al., 2007; Ishii and Mombaerts, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Molecular diversification of Gnao1 neurons occurs due to combinatorial co-expression of H2-Mv genes along with V2Rs.
source: In addition, further molecular diversification of Gnao1 neurons occurs due to combinatorial co-expression of a family of non-classical Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) genes, H2-Mv, that are co-expressed along with V2Rs (Ishii et al., 2003; Loconto et al., 2003, Ishii and Mombaerts, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A few combinations of V2R and H2-Mv expression have been identified, indicating that these co-expression patterns are non-random and could be functionally important.
source: A few combinations of V2R and H2-Mv expression have been identified, indicating that these co-expression patterns are non-random and could be functionally important (Martini et al., 2001; Ishii et al., 2003; Loconto et al., 2003; Silvotti et al., 2007; Ishii and Mombaerts, 2008; Ishii and Mombaerts, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Recent studies using single-cell transcriptomic analysis have implicated Notch signaling along with downstream transcription factors, Tfap2e, Bcl11b to play a role in specifying the fates of developing VSNs.
source: Recent studies using single-cell transcriptomic analysis have implicated Notch signaling along with downstream transcription factors, Tfap2e, Bcl11b to play a role in specifying the fates of developing VSNs (Enomoto et al., 2011; Katreddi et al., 2022; Lin et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The study retained 9185 cells from all samples for analysis after quality control steps.
source: Initial quality control steps were performed (see methods) to remove cells with high or low total RNA content and red blood cell contamination, resulting in the retention of 9185 cells from all samples for further analysis.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data processing in the study.

claim: Comparison of gene expression obtained from male versus female mice did not reveal appreciable differences other than known sexually dimorphic genes.
source: Since our comparison of gene expression obtained from male versus female mice, did not reveal appreciable differences other than known sexually dimorphic genes that include Eif2s3y, Ddx3y, Uty, and Kdm5d (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), we pooled cells from both sexes for further analysis.
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 1 shows the comparison between male and female samples.

claim: Dimensionality reduction and unsupervised clustering resulted in 18 distinct clusters.
source: To group cells based on their gene expression profiles, we performed dimensionality reduction and unsupervised clustering, which resulted in 18 distinct clusters (Figure 1A), with gene expression markers specific to each cluster (Figure 1B).
evidence: Figure 1A shows the UMAP with 18 clusters.

claim: 63.7 percent (5852 cells) of the 9185 cells were neuronal cell types at different developmental stages.
source: Amongst 9185 cells, we observed that 63.7 percent (5852 cells) were neuronal cell types at different developmental stages which includes progenitor cells (Cluster 5; defined by expression of Ascl1, Neurod1, Neurog1), immature neurons (Cluster12; expression of Gap43), Gnao1 neurons (Cluster 14; based on expression of Gnao1, V2Rs), and Gnai2 neurons (Cluster 7, 16; characterized by Gnai2, V1Rs expression) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the clustering analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: 36.3 percent of cells were classified to be of non-neuronal types.
source: The remaining 36.3 percent of cells were classified to be of non-neuronal types which include sustentacular cells (Cluster 15; defined by Cyp2a5, Ppic), cells from non-sensory epithelium (Cluster 11; defined by Ly6d, Krt5), cells from glandular tissue (Cluster 13; characterized by Obp2a, Lcn3), immune cells which include macrophages (Cluster 8, 6, 10; defined by C1qa, C1qb, H2-Aa), T cells (Cluster 9; defined by Cd3d, Cd3g), neutrophils (Cluster 2; defined by s100a8, s100a9), olfactory ensheathing cells (Cluster 3; defined by Gfap, Plp1, Sox10), endothelial cells (cluster 1 and 17; defined by Gng11, Egfl7, Eng), fibroblasts (Cluster 4; defined by Igfbp4, Dcn, Lum) and solitary chemosensory cells (Cluster 18; defined by Trpm5, Gnat3).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the clustering analysis.

claim: Ppic is expressed in sustentacular cells.
source: Thus, we confirmed Ppic to be expressed in sustentacular cells and Ly6d in cells of non-sensory epithelium bordering the VNO lumen.
evidence: Figure 2A shows RNA-ISH validation of Ppic expression in sustentacular cells.

claim: Ly6d is expressed in cells of non-sensory epithelium bordering the VNO lumen.
source: Thus, we confirmed Ppic to be expressed in sustentacular cells and Ly6d in cells of non-sensory epithelium bordering the VNO lumen.
evidence: Figure 2A shows RNA-ISH validation of Ly6d expression.

claim: Ppic and Ly6d are better markers to distinguish sustentacular cells from non-sensory epithelium than Cbr2.
source: Since, Cbr2 - a known marker of sustentacular cells is also expressed in the non-sensory epithelium (Figure 1C), Ppic and Ly6d are better markers to distinguish them.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression patterns observed in Figure 1C.

claim: Obp2a is expressed in cells from glandular tissue on the non-sensory side.
source: Obp2a was confirmed to be expressed in cells from glandular tissue on the non-sensory side.
evidence: Figure 2A shows RNA-ISH validation of Obp2a expression.

claim: Plp1 and Mgp are expressed in cells located at the periphery of the neuro-epithelium.
source: Plp1 and Mgp, markers of olfactory ensheathing glial cells and endothelial cells/fibroblasts, respectively, were observed to be expressed in cells located at the periphery of the neuro-epithelium.
evidence: Figure 2A shows RNA-ISH validation of Plp1 and Mgp expression.

claim: Macrophage cell markers C1qb and H2-Aa are expressed in scattered cells throughout the neuroepithelium.
source: Macrophage cell markers C1qb and H2-Aa were observed to be specifically expressed in scattered cells throughout the neuroepithelium, with H2-Aa co-expression also seen in sustentacular cells (Figure 2A), confirming the presence of these cell types within the neuroepithelium.
evidence: Figure 2A shows RNA-ISH validation of C1qb and H2-Aa expression.

claim: Three clusters of macrophage-like cells were identified based on the expression of C1qa, C1qb, C1qc, and MHC class II gene H2-Aa.
source: Three clusters (Figure 1A, clusters 6, 8, 10 termed as Mac1, Mac2, Mac3, respectively) comprised of macrophage-like cells based on the expression of C1qa, C1qb, C1qc, and MHC class II gene - H2-Aa (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: Figure 2B and C show the UMAP and dot plot of macrophage clusters.

claim: Cluster 10 (Mac3) expresses classical microglial markers such as Tmem119, Aif1 (Iba1), P2ry12, Cx3cr1, Trem2, along with chemokine genes Ccl3, Ccl4, and Ccl7 and Interleukins Il1a, Il1b.
source: Further analysis indicates that cluster 10 (Mac3) expresses classical microglial markers such as Tmem119, Aif1 (Iba1), P2ry12, Cx3cr1, Trem2, along with chemokine genes - Ccl3, Ccl4, and Ccl7 and Interleukins – Il1a, Il1b (Figure 2C), indicating an activated macrophage subset.
evidence: Figure 2C shows the dot plot with expression of these markers in Mac3.

claim: Cluster 8 (Mac2) is similar to Mac3 in regard to expression of classical tissue-resident macrophage marker Adgre1 (F4/80), C1qa, C1qb, C1qc but lacks expression of chemokine and interleukin genes.
source: Cluster 8 (Mac2) is similar to Mac3 in regard to expression of classical tissue-resident macrophage marker - Adgre1 (F4/80), C1qa, C1qb, C1qc but lacks expression of chemokine and interleukin genes mentioned earlier.
evidence: Figure 2C shows the expression patterns of these markers.

claim: Mac1 cluster is distinguished by the lack of C1qa, C1qb, Cd68, Adgre1(F4/80), and microglial markers but possesses high levels of Napsa, Lsp1, H2-Aa.
source: In comparison to Mac3 and Mac2, the Mac 1 cluster is distinguished by the lack of C1qa, C1qb, Cd68, Adgre1(F4/80), and microglial markers but possesses high levels of Napsa, Lsp1, H2-Aa (Figure 2C, Supplementary file 1 and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Figure 2C shows the expression patterns of these markers.

claim: The study did not observe evidence via RNA-ISH for T-cell markers (Cd3d, Cd3g), raising the possibility that these immune cell types may have co-purified from blood.
source: On the other hand, we did not observe evidence via RNA-ISH for T-cell markers (Cd3d, Cd3g), raising the possibility that these immune cell types may have co-purified from blood.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of RNA-ISH validation for T-cell markers.

claim: The study identified expression of Trpm5 and Gnat3 genes that mark solitary chemosensory cells expressing taste receptors and related markers.
source: Lastly, we were able to identify via RNA-ISH, the expression of Trpm5 (Figure 2A) and Gnat3 genes from our dataset, that mark solitary chemosensory cells expressing taste receptors and related markers (Ogura et al., 2010; Supplementary file 1), indicating that rare cell-populations were captured, and their markers identified in our study.
evidence: Figure 2A shows RNA-ISH validation of Trpm5 expression, and the claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Re-clustering of neuronal cell types resulted in 13 clusters (labeled n1-n13).
source: In order to obtain a better resolution on neuronal sub-types, We pooled cells from clusters representing neuronal types identified in Figure 1 (clusters 5, 7, 12, 14, 16), created a new Seurat object, and performed re-clustering. This resulted in 13 clusters (labeled n1-n13), which potentially represent distinct neuronal sub-populations within the broadly defined Gnao1 and Gnai2 neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 1A shows the UMAP with 13 neuronal clusters.

claim: Cluster n5 represents Globose basal cells defined by Ascl1 expression.
source: Since neurogenesis is a continuous process in VNO neurons (Barber and Raisman, 1978; Wilson and Raisman, 1980), these clusters also represent a snapshot of cells at different developmental states, identified by known markers: Globose basal cells (Cluster n5; Ascl1), progenitor cells (Cluster n5; defined by expression of Neurod1, Neurog1), immature neurons (Cluster n6, n7; defined by Gap43) expressing Gnao1 or Gnai2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 1B shows the expression of Ascl1 in cluster n5.

claim: Cluster n5 represents progenitor cells defined by expression of Neurod1 and Neurog1.
source: Since neurogenesis is a continuous process in VNO neurons (Barber and Raisman, 1978; Wilson and Raisman, 1980), these clusters also represent a snapshot of cells at different developmental states, identified by known markers: Globose basal cells (Cluster n5; Ascl1), progenitor cells (Cluster n5; defined by expression of Neurod1, Neurog1), immature neurons (Cluster n6, n7; defined by Gap43) expressing Gnao1 or Gnai2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 1B shows the expression of Neurod1 and Neurog1 in cluster n5.

claim: Clusters n6 and n7 represent immature neurons defined by Gap43 expression.
source: Since neurogenesis is a continuous process in VNO neurons (Barber and Raisman, 1978; Wilson and Raisman, 1980), these clusters also represent a snapshot of cells at different developmental states, identified by known markers: Globose basal cells (Cluster n5; Ascl1), progenitor cells (Cluster n5; defined by expression of Neurod1, Neurog1), immature neurons (Cluster n6, n7; defined by Gap43) expressing Gnao1 or Gnai2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 1B shows the expression of Gap43 in clusters n6 and n7.

claim: Among Gap43 negative mature neurons, Gnao1 neurons are clusters n1-n4.
source: Among Gap43 negative mature neurons, Gnao1 neurons are clusters n1-n4, (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B, corresponding to cluster 14 in Figure 1A), where sub-cluster identity is clearly defined by their co-expression of H2-Mv and Vmn2r GPCRs (discussed in detail in the co-expression section below).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B show the clustering and marker expression.

claim: Six clusters (n8-n13) correspond to mature Gnai2 neurons.
source: In contrast, six clusters (n8-n13) correspond to mature Gnai2 neurons (clusters 7, 16 from Figure 1A), of which n8-n11 do not have any definite gene markers and differ based on differences in the expression level of a few genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 1C shows the marker expression for these clusters.

claim: Neurons of sub-cluster n12 exclusively express genes Tmbim1, Lgi2, Cleg2g.
source: Neurons of sub-cluster n12 (cluster 7 from Figure 1A) exclusively express genes Tmbim1, Lgi2, Cleg2g, and n13 are distinguished by the expression of previously identified activity-dependent genes - Rasgrp4, Pcdh10, and S100a5 (Fischl et al., 2014; Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 1C shows the expression of these markers, and the claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Sub-cluster n13 is distinguished by the expression of activity-dependent genes Rasgrp4, Pcdh10, and S100a5.
source: Neurons of sub-cluster n12 (cluster 7 from Figure 1A) exclusively express genes Tmbim1, Lgi2, Cleg2g, and n13 are distinguished by the expression of previously identified activity-dependent genes - Rasgrp4, Pcdh10, and S100a5 (Fischl et al., 2014; Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 1C shows the expression of these markers, and the claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Exclusion of VRs from clustering parameters did not affect the divergence of mature neurons into Gnai2/Gnao1.
source: Exclusion of VRs from clustering parameters did not affect the divergence of mature neurons into Gnai2 /Gnao1 and only selectively affected some of the subclusters (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), thus indicating that neuronal subtype identity was governed by gene expression differences beyond vomeronasal GPCRs.
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 2 shows the clustering results with and without VRs.

claim: Neuronal subtype identity is governed by gene expression differences beyond vomeronasal GPCRs.
source: Exclusion of VRs from clustering parameters did not affect the divergence of mature neurons into Gnai2 /Gnao1 and only selectively affected some of the subclusters (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), thus indicating that neuronal subtype identity was governed by gene expression differences beyond vomeronasal GPCRs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the clustering results shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pseudo-time analysis confirms a split of immature Gap43+ neurons into Gnao1 or Gnai2 cell clusters.
source: The trajectory of development confirms a split of immature Gap43 +neurons into Gnao1 or Gnai2 cell clusters (Figure 3A).
evidence: Figure 3A shows the pseudotime trajectory with the developmental split.

claim: Multiple genes that are known transcription regulators but not previously reported to be enriched in Gnao1 neurons were found, including Creb5, Prrxl1, Shisa8, Lmo4, and Foxo1.
source: To our surprise, we found multiple genes that are known transcription regulators but are not previously reported to be enriched in Gnao1 neurons. These include Creb5, Prrxl1, Shisa8, Lmo4, and Foxo1.
evidence: Figure 3B and C show the differential expression and feature plots of these transcription factors.

claim: Creb5 and Prrxl1 are transcription factors expressed only in immature Gnao1 neurons.
source: Creb5, Prrxl1 are transcription factors expressed only in immature Gnao1 neurons whereas Shisa8, Lmo4, and Foxo1 expression is enriched in immature Gnao1 neurons compared to mature ones (Figure 3C).
evidence: Figure 3C shows the feature plots indicating the restricted expression of Creb5 and Prrxl1 to immature neurons.

claim: Shisa8, Lmo4, and Foxo1 expression is enriched in immature Gnao1 neurons compared to mature ones.
source: Creb5, Prrxl1 are transcription factors expressed only in immature Gnao1 neurons whereas Shisa8, Lmo4, and Foxo1 expression is enriched in immature Gnao1 neurons compared to mature ones (Figure 3C).
evidence: Figure 3C shows the feature plots indicating enrichment in immature neurons.

claim: Prrxl1 was reported to auto-repress its expression which explains how its expression is limited to immature Gnao1 neurons.
source: Prrxl1 was reported to auto-repress its expression which explains how its expression is limited to immature Gnao1 neurons (Monteiro et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The developmental transition of VNO neurons to Gnao1 lineage may involve the transient expression of transcription factors within immature neurons after dichotomy is established.
source: These data indicate that the developmental transition of VNO neurons to Gnao1 lineage may involve the transient expression of transcription factors within immature neurons after dichotomy is established.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed transient expression patterns of transcription factors.

claim: Four Gnao1 neuron clusters (n1-n4) are organized majorly based on the expression of family-C V2Rs and H2-Mv genes, especially Vmn2r1 or Vmn2r2.
source: These four clusters (Figure 4A) are found to be organized majorly based on the expression of family-C V2Rs and H2-Mv genes, especially Vmn2r1 or Vmn2r2 (Figure 4B–E).
evidence: Figure 4B-E show the expression patterns of Vmn2r1, Vmn2r2, and H2-Mv genes across the clusters.

claim: Cluster n1 and cluster n4 express Vmn2r1.
source: Of the four clusters, cluster n1 and cluster n4 express Vmn2r1 (Figure 4B and E) whereas cluster n3 neurons are distinguished by the co-expression of Vmn2r2 along with other family-C members (Vmn2r3, Vmn2r4, Vmn2r5, Vmn2r6, Vmn2r7) (Figure 4C and E).
evidence: Figure 4B and E show the expression of Vmn2r1 in clusters n1 and n4.

claim: Cluster n3 neurons are distinguished by the co-expression of Vmn2r2 along with other family-C members (Vmn2r3, Vmn2r4, Vmn2r5, Vmn2r6, Vmn2r7).
source: Of the four clusters, cluster n1 and cluster n4 express Vmn2r1 (Figure 4B and E) whereas cluster n3 neurons are distinguished by the co-expression of Vmn2r2 along with other family-C members (Vmn2r3, Vmn2r4, Vmn2r5, Vmn2r6, Vmn2r7) (Figure 4C and E).
evidence: Figure 4C and E show the co-expression of Vmn2r2 with other family-C members in cluster n3.

claim: Cluster n2 is a mixture of either Vmn2r1 or Vmn2r2 expressing neurons.
source: Cluster n2 is a mixture of either Vmn2r1 or Vmn2r2 expressing neurons (Figure 4E), with Vmn2r2 being similarly co-expressed along with other family-C members in those cells.
evidence: Figure 4E shows the heatmap with expression of Vmn2r1 and Vmn2r2 in cluster n2.

claim: Among family-ABDE members, A1-A6 V2Rs are highly expressed in cluster n2, n3 which co-express Vmn2r2.
source: We observed that among family-ABDE members, A1-A6 V2Rs are highly expressed in cluster n2, n3 which co-express Vmn2r2 whereas A8-A10, B, D, and E family V2Rs are mainly expressed along with Vmn2r1 in cluster n1 neurons (Figure 4E).
evidence: Figure 4E shows the heatmap with expression patterns of V2R families.

claim: A8-A10, B, D, and E family V2Rs are mainly expressed along with Vmn2r1 in cluster n1 neurons.
source: We observed that among family-ABDE members, A1-A6 V2Rs are highly expressed in cluster n2, n3 which co-express Vmn2r2 whereas A8-A10, B, D, and E family V2Rs are mainly expressed along with Vmn2r1 in cluster n1 neurons (Figure 4E).
evidence: Figure 4E shows the heatmap with expression patterns of V2R families.

claim: These observations of family biased expression of ABDE with Vmn2r1 or Vmn2r2 agrees with earlier studies.
source: These observations of family biased expression of ABDE with Vmn2r1 or Vmn2r2 agrees with earlier studies (Silvotti et al., 2007; Silvotti et al., 2011) that have used antibody or RNA probe based approaches.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Expression of H2-Mv genes (H2-M10.1, H2-M10.2, H2-M10.3, H2-M10.4, H2-M10.5, H2-M10.6) is largely confined to clusters n2 and n3, where they are co-expressed selectively in Vmn2r2 positive neurons and mostly absent from Vmn2r1 expressing cluster n1, n2 neurons.
source: Furthermore, we observed that expression of H2-Mv genes (H2-M10.1, H2-M10.2, H2-M10.3, H2-M10.4, H2-M10.5, H2-M10.6) is largely confined to clusters n2 and n3, where they are co-expressed selectively in Vmn2r2 positive neurons and mostly absent from Vmn2r1 expressing cluster n1, n2 neurons (Figure 4D and E, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Figure 4D and E show the expression patterns of H2-Mv genes.

claim: These observations align with prior reports from antibody or RNA probe-based experiments, that demonstrated a sub-division amongst Gnao1 neurons based on their expression of family-C Vmn2rs and co-expression of H2-Mv genes with the Vmn2r2 subset.
source: These observations align with prior reports from antibody or RNA probe-based experiments, that demonstrated a sub-division amongst Gnao1 neurons based on their expression of family-C Vmn2rs and co-expression of H2-Mv genes with the Vmn2r2 subset (Silvotti et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Family C1 V2R (Vmn2r1) is mostly expressed alone without any other family-C members.
source: Within the expression patterns represented by a frequency of more than two cells, we observed that family C1 V2R (Vmn2r1) is mostly expressed alone without any other family-C members (Figure 4F and E) as shown earlier (Silvotti et al., 2007).
evidence: Figure 4F shows the bar plot of family-C V2R co-expression, and the claim is supported by a citation.

claim: A few cells (31 neurons out of 1025 Gnao1 neurons) were observed to co-express Vmn2r1 along with Vmn2r7.
source: Surprisingly a few cells (31 neurons out of 1025 Gnao1 neurons) were observed to co-express Vmn2r1 along with Vmn2r7 (Supplementary file 5), contrary to earlier reports that Vmn2r1 does not co-express with family-C2 receptors.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the co-expression analysis.

claim: Most of Gnao1 neurons with family C2 V2Rs (Vmn2r2-Vmn2r7) co-express multiple members amongst them, ranging from 2 to 6 V2Rs per cell.
source: Most of Gnao1 neurons with family C2 V2Rs (Vmn2r2-Vmn2r7) co-express multiple members amongst them, ranging from 2 to 6 V2Rs per cell (Figure 4F and E).
evidence: Figure 4F shows the bar plot of family-C V2R co-expression.

claim: Most Gnao1 neurons follow the 'one ABD-V2R, one neuron' rule, except for a few that express two ABD-V2Rs.
source: In the case of family-ABD V2R expression, we observed that most Gnao1 neurons follow the 'one ABD-V2R, one neuron' rule, except for a few that express two ABD-V2Rs (Figure 4G).
evidence: Figure 4G shows the bar plot of family-ABD V2R co-expression.

claim: Amongst cells that express more than two ABD-V2Rs, the combination of Vmn2r20 and Vmn2r22 stood out as the highest (44 cells), followed by Vmn2r39, Vmn2r43, and Vmn2r50 (10 cells).
source: Amongst cells that express more than two ABD-V2Rs, the combination of Vmn2r20 and Vmn2r22 stood out as the highest (44 cells), followed by Vmn2r39, Vmn2r43, and Vmn2r50 (10 cells, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the co-expression analysis.

claim: Among Gnao1 neurons (n1-n4), 229 cells did not express family-C V2Rs as per the threshold.
source: Among Gnao1 neurons (n1-n4), 229 cells did not express family-C V2Rs (Figure 4F) and 46 cells did not express ABD-V2Rs (Figure 4G) as per our threshold.
evidence: Figure 4F shows the bar plot with cells expressing 0 family-C V2Rs.

claim: Among Gnao1 neurons (n1-n4), 46 cells did not express ABD-V2Rs as per the threshold.
source: Among Gnao1 neurons (n1-n4), 229 cells did not express family-C V2Rs (Figure 4F) and 46 cells did not express ABD-V2Rs (Figure 4G) as per our threshold.
evidence: Figure 4G shows the bar plot with cells expressing 0 ABD-V2Rs.

evidence: Figure 4—figure supplement 4C shows the box plot comparing total V1R and Gnai2 expression.

claim: 924 differentially expressed genes were identified between mature Gnao1 and Gnai2 neurons with at least log2 fold change of 1 and adjusted p-value <10e-6.
source: Since the exclusion of VR genes did not fundamentally alter the clustering and divergence into mature Gnai2 /Gnao1 neurons, we decided to investigate the gene expression differences between these neurons by performing differential gene expression analysis of mature Gnao1 (cluster 14 from Figure 1) and Gnai2 neurons (cluster 7, 16 from Figure 1) and identified 924 differentially expressed genes with at least log2 fold change of 1 and adjusted p-value <10e-6.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Of the 924 differentially expressed genes, 456 genes are enriched in Gnao1 neurons and 468 genes in Gnai2 neurons.
source: Of these, 456 genes are enriched in Gnao1 neurons and 468 genes in Gnai2 neurons (Figure 5A).

evidence: Figure 5D shows the RNA-ISH validation of Tppp3 and Gm36028 expression.

claim: Ckb is enriched in Gnai2 neurons and also expressed in sustentacular cells.
source: Some of the enriched genes such as Ckb in Gnai2 and Krt18 in Gnao1 neurons, were also observed to be expressed in sustentacular cells (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: Figure 5C shows the RNA-ISH validation of Ckb expression.

claim: Krt18 is enriched in Gnao1 neurons and also expressed in sustentacular cells.

evidence: Figure 5D shows the RNA-ISH validation of Krt18 expression.

source: Furthermore, from chromogenic RNA-ISH experiments, we observed genes such as Nsg1, Rtp1, Dner, Qpct, Pcdh7 to be either restricted to or highly expressed in Gnai2 neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) and others such as Apmap, Selenof, Hspa5, Itm2b, Agpat5 were observed to have a gradient of high to low-level expression from Gnao1 to Gnai2 zones (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Prph is specifically expressed in scattered subsets of Gnai2 neurons.
source: Two genes: Sncg and Prph specifically expressed in scattered subsets of Gnao1 or Gnai2 neurons, respectively, (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B) indicating selective expression in a particular neuronal subpopulation.
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1A shows the RNA-ISH validation of Prph expression.

claim: VNO neurons that start from a common progenitor, go on to transiently express genes during immature stages that could decide their cell fate and these cells exhibit markedly different gene expression profiles in the mature stage.
source: Taken together our data indicate that VNO neurons that start from a common progenitor, go on to transiently express genes during immature stages that could decide their cell fate and these cells exhibit markedly different gene expression profiles in the mature stage.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the developmental trajectory and differential expression analyses.

claim: Gene ontology enrichment analysis of Gnao1 neuron genes shows that most of the enriched terms with p-value <0.05 are related to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) processes.
source: Interestingly, we observed that amongst the Gnao1 neuron genes, most of the enriched terms with p-value <0.05, are related to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) processes, which include 'protein folding,' 'response to ER stress,' and 'ERAD pathway' (Figure 6A).
evidence: Figure 6A shows the GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: Gene ontology analysis of Gnai2 neuron genes did not reveal any particular enrichment of GO terms in this neuronal subset.
source: Conversely, a gene ontology analysis of Gnai2 neuron genes did not reveal any particular enrichment of GO terms in this neuronal subset.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of the GO analysis.

claim: More than 20% of the genes associated with protein folding are enriched in Gnao1 neurons.
source: As more than 20% of the genes associated with protein folding (Figure 6A) are enriched in Gnao1 neurons, we sought to probe the spatial transcription pattern of some of the candidates.
evidence: Figure 6A shows the GO enrichment analysis with gene counts.

claim: Fluorescence RNA in-situ hybridization confirmed the selective expression of ER genes such as Creld2, Dnajc3, Pdia6, and Sdf2l1 amongst Gnao1 neurons.
source: Fluorescence RNA in-situ hybridization confirmed the selective expression of ER genes such as Creld2, Dnajc3, Pdia6, and Sdf2l1 amongst Gnao1 neurons (Figure 6B).
evidence: Figure 6B shows the RNA-ISH validation of ER gene expression.

claim: Anti-SEKDEL antibody intensely labeled Gnao1 neurons.
source: We first tried an antibody against SEKDEL, a common ER retention signal, which intensely labeled Gnao1 neurons (Figure 7A).
evidence: Figure 7A shows the immunofluorescence image with anti-SEKDEL labeling.

claim: Selective labeling of SEKDEL in Gnao1 neurons was confirmed by co-labeling with anti-Gnao1.
source: This selective labeling was confirmed by co-labeling with anti-Gnao1 (Figure 7B and D), where an anti-SEKDEL ER signal is seen in Gnao1 neurons.
evidence: Figure 7B and D show the co-labeling with anti-Gnao1.

claim: Enrichment of SEKDEL was quantified across multiple (26) VNO sections from three mice, labeled with anti-SEKDEL, anti-Gnao1, and anti-Omp as a control.
source: We quantified enrichment of SEKDEL across multiple (26) VNO sections from three mice, labeled with anti-SEKDEL, anti-Gnao1, and anti-Omp as a control.
evidence: This is a description of the quantification method.

source: Normalized fluorescence intensity quantified along the apical-basal axis (Figure 7D and E), shows that SEKDEL signal intensity increases along with Gnao1.
evidence: Figure 7E shows the quantification plot.

claim: Several antibodies that detect ER chaperone proteins (Hspa5 (BiP), PDI, Grp94, Calnexin) show enrichment in Gnao1 neurons.
source: Surprisingly, several other antibodies that detect ER chaperone proteins: Hspa5 (BiP), PDI, Grp94, Calnexin (Figure 7F, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A); as well as antibodies against ER membrane/structural proteins: Sec61β, Atlastin1, NogoB, Climp63, Reep5 (Goyal and Blackstone, 2013) show a similar enrichment in Gnao1 neurons, as seen from the immune-fluorescence images and their quantification with Gnao1 or SEKDEL antibodies (Figure 7G and H, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Figure 7F and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A show the immunofluorescence images and quantification.

claim: Antibodies against ER membrane/structural proteins (Sec61β, Atlastin1, NogoB, Climp63, Reep5) show enrichment in Gnao1 neurons.
source: Surprisingly, several other antibodies that detect ER chaperone proteins: Hspa5 (BiP), PDI, Grp94, Calnexin (Figure 7F, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A); as well as antibodies against ER membrane/structural proteins: Sec61β, Atlastin1, NogoB, Climp63, Reep5 (Goyal and Blackstone, 2013) show a similar enrichment in Gnao1 neurons, as seen from the immune-fluorescence images and their quantification with Gnao1 or SEKDEL antibodies (Figure 7G and H, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Figure 7G, H, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B show the immunofluorescence images and quantification, and the claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Some ER protein localizations (SEKDEL, Hspa5, PDI, Atlastin1, NogoB) were detected selectively amongst basal zone Gnao1 neurons.
source: Some ER protein localizations (SEKDEL, Hspa5, PDI, Atlastin1, NogoB) were detected selectively amongst basal zone Gnao1 neurons, while others (Sec61β, Calnexin, Grp94, Reep5, Climp63) detected a pattern of Gnao1 neuron enrichment, with lower levels in Gnai2 neurons.
evidence: This is a summary of the immunofluorescence observations.

claim: Some ER proteins (Sec61β, Calnexin, Grp94, Reep5, Climp63) detected a pattern of Gnao1 neuron enrichment, with lower levels in Gnai2 neurons.
source: Some ER protein localizations (SEKDEL, Hspa5, PDI, Atlastin1, NogoB) were detected selectively amongst basal zone Gnao1 neurons, while others (Sec61β, Calnexin, Grp94, Reep5, Climp63) detected a pattern of Gnao1 neuron enrichment, with lower levels in Gnai2 neurons.
evidence: This is a summary of the immunofluorescence observations.

evidence: Figure 7—figure supplement 2 shows the violin plots comparing RNA levels, and references to Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

source: On the other hand, RNA levels of Atlastin1, and PDI were comparable (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), indicating that Gnao1 neuron enrichment of some ER proteins could also arise due to post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms.

claim: Gnao1 neuron enrichment of some ER proteins could arise due to post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms.
source: On the other hand, RNA levels of Atlastin1, and PDI were comparable (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), indicating that Gnao1 neuron enrichment of some ER proteins could also arise due to post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that protein levels are enriched but RNA levels are comparable.

claim: Serial sections (70 nm thick) of ~1 mm square regions of the VNO were collected on tape and were imaged by scanning electron microscopy.
source: Serial sections (70 nm thick) of ~1 mm square regions of the VNO were collected on tape and were imaged by scanning electron microscopy (Baena et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a description of the electron microscopy method, supported by a citation.

claim: Gnai2 cells were distinguished from Gnao1 cells by their location as they are spatially segregated into apical or basal zones, respectively, within the neuroepithelium.
source: Since the sections contained the entire VNO, we were able to distinguish Gnai2 from Gnao1 cells by their location as they are spatially segregated into apical or basal zones, respectively, within the neuroepithelium (Figure 8A).
evidence: Figure 8A shows the electron micrograph with labeled zones.

claim: In Gnao1 cells, more than half of the cytoplasm contained dense smooth ER with cubic membrane morphology.
source: In Gnao1 cells, more than half of the cytoplasm contained dense smooth ER with cubic membrane morphology (Almsherqi et al., 2006; Almsherqi et al., 2009), also known as organized smooth ER (OSER) (Snapp et al., 2003; Figure 8A and B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 8A, B, and Figure 8—figure supplement 1 show the electron micrographs, and the claim is supported by citations.

claim: In the remainder of the cytoplasm of Gnao1 cells, there were closely apposed parallel sheets of ER membrane that were contiguous with lamellar ER surrounding the nucleus.
source: In the remainder of the cytoplasm, there were closely apposed parallel sheets of ER membrane that were contiguous with lamellar ER surrounding the nucleus (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 8—figure supplement 1 shows the electron micrograph.

claim: The apical/Gnai2 neuronal cell bodies are smaller than those of Gnao1 cell bodies.
source: The apical/Gnai2 neuronal cell bodies are smaller than those of Gnao1 cell bodies.
evidence: This is an observation from the electron microscopy images.

claim: Gnai2 neurons appeared to have cubic ER membranes, but these seemed denser and occupied a smaller fraction of cytoplasmic volume compared to Gnao1 neurons.
source: They also appeared to have cubic ER membranes, but these seemed denser and occupied a smaller fraction of cytoplasmic volume (Figure 8A and C).
evidence: Figure 8A and C show the electron micrographs comparing Gnao1 and Gnai2 neurons.

claim: Mature Gnao1 neurons differ substantially from Gnai2 neurons in selectively upregulating the transcription of several ER genes.
source: Taken together, our data indicates that mature Gnao1 neurons differ substantially from Gnai2 neurons in selectively upregulating the transcription of several ER genes.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the transcriptomic and validation data.

source: Furthermore, this neuronal subset also exhibits higher levels of ER proteins, via transcriptional and post-transcriptional mechanisms, as well as a hypertrophic smooth ER that is arranged in the form of an organized cubic membrane ultrastructure.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the immunofluorescence and electron microscopy data.

evidence: This is a summary inference based on the electron microscopy data.

source: Most Importantly, a critical period of Notch signaling determines whether progenitors give rise to apical, basal, or sustentacular cell types.

source: After Gnao1/Gnai2 identity is established, transcription factor Tfap2e, continuously expressed from immature to mature Gnao1 neurons, is required to maintain the Gnao1 fate (Lin et al., 2018; Lin et al., 2022; Katreddi et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

source: Pseudo-time analysis of our data confirmed a developmental trajectory that starts with progenitor cells, leading to immature neurons that take on either Gnai2 or Gnao1 fate.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

source: Our observations on the tight temporal regulation of these transcription factor-related genes in the developmental trajectory of Gnao1 neurons indicate that additional molecular players might be important in further specification or maintenance of this neuronal lineage.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed expression patterns.

claim: Some V1Rs were found to consistently co-express in Gnai2 neurons and the major combinations observed from the analysis match those identified recently from a functional single-cell study.
source: Some V1Rs were found to consistently co-express in Gnai2 neurons and the major combinations observed from our analysis (such as Vmn1r85/86, Figure 4—figure supplement 4), match those identified recently from a functional single-cell study (Lee et al., 2019), leading confidence to the methodology used in our co-expression analysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The analysis of family-C, family ABD-V2Rs and H2-Mv genes expressed per cell, confirmed the earlier reported sub-division of basal/Gnao1 neurons into those that express either Vmn2r1 (family-C1) or Vmn2r2-Vmn2r7 (family-C2).
source: In our study, the analysis of family-C, family ABD-V2Rs and H2-Mv genes expressed per cell, confirmed the earlier reported sub-division of basal/Gnao1 neurons into those that express either Vmn2r1 (family-C1) or Vmn2r2-Vmn2r7 (family-C2), resulting in a broad four-part division of mature VNO neurons: those expressing (a) Gnai2/V1Rs, (b) Gnao1/Vmn2r1, (c) Gnao1/Vmn2r2-2r7; H2-Mv+, (d) Gnao1/Vmn2r2-2r7; H2-Mv-.
evidence: This is a summary of the co-expression analysis results.

claim: The co-expression of ABD-V2R sub-families A1-A5 and most of the H2-Mv genes with Vmn2r2/family-C2 neurons as well as preferential co-expression of A6-A9, B, D, E sub-families with Vmn2r1 along with exclusion of H2Mv genes from these neurons, points to the overall non-random logic of V2R/H2Mv co-expression.
